correctness.rationale: A fully specified elementary Dirichlet-simplex transformation establishes the one-subset event with exact uniform coefficient and Lipschitz nonuniform error. Conditioning on a shared anchor bounds every intersecting-pair joint event by C epsilon^(2m-k-1). Independent disjoint-label events allow classical dependency-graph Poisson approximation; overlap sums have worst order n^(-1/(m-1)), and intensity differs from its limit by O(n^-1). The zero-count identity proves the Weibull law; threshold endpoints and m=2 were verified. The 321 finite assertions and 390000 seeded Bernoulli trials are corroboration, not replacements for analytical proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected first public motivating paper addresses anchored lines, the standard broad circle U-max result requires a smooth Hessian, and two closely related published circle findings address fixed-size Rips topology or short consecutive scan clusters. The regular-polygon density product and harmonic resonance were previously established in another model and are credited, not presented as independently novel. No inspected claim implies the growing-n Poisson count and optimal min-gap Weibull law. Residual historical priority uncertainty is acknowledged.
residual_risks: No exhaustive historical search of all probabilistic circle-packing, cyclic dispersion, and extreme U-statistics literature was possible; an implicit statement-level equivalent may exist.

General older Poisson U-max machinery is not new. Priority is attached only to the min-gap small-deficit coefficient with explicit overlapping-subset rates and the resulting fixed-m circular selection limit.
No independent reviewer has inspected the proof; same-model verification is not independent certification.
